question: Should OpenClaw core permanently own gateway-local multi-user identity, authorization, persistent grants, member device pairing, and the restricted Teams portal introduced by this PR?
rationale: Implementation review cannot decide whether this broad new product and security boundary belongs in core, especially where repository policy otherwise routes optional service workflows and owner-specific behavior through plugins or separate owner surfaces.

options.title: Narrow to extension seams
options.body: Keep only proven generic core or plugin-API gaps and move the optional Teams identity, portal, and policy product to its own maintained plugin or product surface.

options.title: Sponsor the core boundary
options.body: Accept core ownership with named gateway, security, plugin-SDK, Workspaces, and web-UI reviewers plus a threat model, upgrade proof, and live adversarial validation.

options.title: Pause the proposal
options.body: Defer or close the branch until maintainers sponsor a concrete architecture and long-term ownership model.

recommendation.title: Narrow to extension seams
recommendation.body: Keep only proven generic core or plugin-API gaps and move the optional Teams identity, portal, and policy product to its own maintained plugin or product surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The person authored the current merged Workspaces foundation and is the strongest available routing candidate for deciding whether its scope should expand into a core multi-user product.
